paper_title: Seasonality in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
selected_experiment: Table 2, equal-weighted decile portfolios sorted on average return at annual lags 24, 36, 48 and 60 months (Years 2-5 Annual strategy), decile 10 minus decile 1

economic_rationale.value: Persistent seasonal variation in expected returns: individual stocks earn systematically different (high or low) expected returns in particular calendar months every year, so past same-calendar-month winners keep earning high returns in that month

evidence.quote: This result is consistent with individual stocks that persistently earn different returns over different calendar months within our sample.

universe_and_filters.value: NYSE/AMEX-listed firms with data on the CRSP monthly returns file; holding months January 1965 to December 2002 (456 months), lagged returns back to January 1945; stocks must have return data in the formation months (no other filters stated)

evidence.quote: Our sample includes NYSE/AMEX-listed firms whose data is available on the CRSP monthly returns file.
Our sample includes NYSE/AMEX-listed firms whose data is available on the CRSP monthly returns file.

signal_formula_words.value: For holding month t, each stock's average monthly return over the same calendar month in years 2 through 5 before t, i.e. the simple average of its returns at lags 24, 36, 48 and 60 months

evidence.quote: Our annual winner-loser strategies measure historical returns over formation months that match the calendar holding period month.
We form decile portfolios based on the average monthly return of stocks over all months in each lagged interval

formation_window.value: 4 monthly returns: the returns at lags 24, 36, 48 and 60 months (annual lags within years 2-5)

evidence.quote: on past annual returns during years 2 through 5 ranks stocks according to their average returns during the historical lags 24, 36, 48, and 60

skip_window.value: no separate skip stated; the most recent month used is lag 24, so months t-1 to t-23 and all non-annual months between lags 24 and 60 are not used

evidence.quote: sorting only on annual lags 24, 36, 48, and 60
measure the returns over the next month
The stocks in each portfolio are assigned equal weight, and the portfolios are rebalanced monthly.

sort_rule_evidence.quote: We form decile portfolios based on the average monthly return of stocks over all months in each lagged interval

breakpoints.value: equal-count deciles of all sample stocks each month (equal number of stocks in each portfolio)

evidence.quote: Every month stocks are grouped into ten portfolios (with equal number of stocks in each portfolio)

favored_group.value: highest decile (decile 10, winners) of average return at annual lags 24, 36, 48, 60

evidence.quote: Stocks with above-average returns in a given month tend to above-average

disfavored_group.value: lowest decile (decile 1, losers) of average return at annual lags 24, 36, 48, 60

weighting_evidence.quote: The stocks in each portfolio are assigned equal weight

headline_result.value: Years 2-5 annual winner-minus-loser decile spread earns 67 basis points per month (Table 2: 0.0067, t-statistic 5.35), January 1965 to December 2002

evidence.quote: decile 1 winners outperformed decile 10 losers by 67 basis points
